Soy una persona interesada en la innovación, la tecnología y el desarrollo de soluciones que permitan resolver problemas reales. Me motiva trabajar en equipo, aprender constantemente, aportar ideas y transformar proyectos en propuestas concretas que generen un impacto positivo.

Busco formar un equipo comprometido, creativo y con iniciativa, cuyos integrantes tengan ganas de aportar sus conocimientos, asumir desafíos y participar activamente en el crecimiento del proyecto.
summary: AgroNexo is a decision-support platform that helps Argentine farmers choose crop rotations that rebuild soil carbon, reduce erosion and stay profitable under a changing climate. For each field, our Field Shift engine combines 20 years of daily NASA POWER climate (rain, temperature, radiation, root-zone soil moisture), ISRIC SoilGrids soil properties and the MODIS MOD13Q1 NDVI history of the field, which reveals the current practice (bare-soil days, crop cycles per year). It simulates candidate rotations over every climate year with a soil-carbon model calibrated for the Pampas (AMG) plus RUSLE erosion, and ranks them by soil carbon, erosion, ground cover, drought risk and gross margin. It recommends the rotation with the best soil outcome that gives up at most 15% of the best margin, so sustainability never feels like a gamble. Farmers draw their fields on a map, set their priorities (horizon, tillage) and get a clear answer, plus an AI assistant that works by text, voice and photo. Because farm decisions do not end at the gate, AgroNexo shares the same NASA-based insight with suppliers, cooperatives, insurers, contractors, ports and industry, so the whole chain can act before the weather does.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

AgroNexo answers the question every Argentine farmer faces before each season: what should I plant next so my soil gets better, my water lasts and my farm stays profitable? The farmer draws the field on a map (or lets our satellite-assisted tool trace it), chooses a planning horizon (3 to 30 years) and a tillage system, and Field Shift compares rotations such as soy monoculture, wheat/soy, maize/soy, rotations with cover crops or pastures. For each one it shows soil organic carbon over time, erosion, days with bare soil, drought risk and gross margin in USD/ha, with its range across climate years. It recommends the rotation that improves the soil most while giving up at most 15% of the best margin, and explains why in plain language.

HOW IT WORKS

1) Climate: 20 years (2005-2024) of daily NASA POWER data at the field (precipitation, temperature, solar radiation and root-zone soil moisture) give monthly water balance, rainfall erosivity and the yield of each crop limited by the real rain of its cycle. 2) Soil: ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0 (0-30 cm organic carbon, clay, sand, silt and bulk density) sets the initial carbon stock and soil erodibility. 3) Current practice: the MODIS MOD13Q1 NDVI time series (250 m, via ORNL DAAC) detects crop cycles and bare-soil periods, so we compare the recommendation against what the farmer really does today. 4) Model: we simulate every rotation starting in every climate year with the AMG soil-carbon model (Andriulo, Mary and Guerif, calibrated for the Pampas) and RUSLE erosion, then rank by soil outcome and economics. Seasonal outlooks (ECMWF SEAS5 and NOAA ENSO) and 15-day ensemble forecasts add the near-term risk.

BEYOND THE ROTATION

The same NASA data powers the rest of the farm decisions in one place: climate-disaster prevention (hail, frost, flooding, drought) with probabilities compared with 35 years of history, the best day to harvest and when to sell, 25 years of MODIS and VIIRS fire history from FIRMS, flooding seen through clouds with NISAR radar, 30 m HLS imagery and OPERA disturbance alerts, and nutrient maps. An AI assistant answers by text or voice, cites the source of every number and diagnoses photos of crops, pests, weeds, cattle or hail damage. Suppliers, cooperatives, insurers, harvest contractors, ports and industry see the same data from their side, so a hail forecast reaches the farmer, the supplier and the insurer at the same time.

IMPACT

In the Pampas, years of soy monoculture have reduced soil organic carbon and left fields bare for months, exposed to erosion and drought. AgroNexo turns NASA Earth observations into a concrete, field-level choice that shows the farmer the soil gain and the money at stake at the same time, which is what makes a practice change actually happen. Every recommendation shows its data sources and its uncertainty.

TECHNOLOGY

Python (FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, NumPy, OpenCV), React with TypeScript, Vite and Tailwind, Leaflet and OpenStreetMap maps, Three.js for the 3D presentation, and the Claude API for the assistant and image analysis. A pure-Python engine also runs in the browser through Pyodide (WebAssembly). Demo access: open the link and choose any demo user on the login page (one click, no registration).
